stem: Finasteride is used to treat which pair of conditions?

options.label: A
options.text: Benign prostatic hyperplasia and male-pattern baldness
options.misconception: None — finasteride treats BPH and male pattern hair loss.
options.explanation: The label says finasteride treats BPH (prostate enlargement; the label's older term is 'hypertrophy', but it is hyperplasia) and male pattern hair loss.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Assumes a drug for the aging prostate also treats sexual dysfunction.
options.explanation: Erectile dysfunction is treated with PDE-5 inhibitors such as sildenafil; finasteride lowers dihydrotestosterone and can itself cause sexual dysfunction.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Confuses a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor with testosterone replacement.
options.explanation: Low testosterone needs testosterone replacement; finasteride blocks conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone and can cause gynecomastia.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Treats all hair loss as androgen-driven.
options.explanation: Alopecia areata and vitiligo are autoimmune and treated with corticosteroids or JAK inhibitors; finasteride targets androgen-driven hair loss instead.

options.label: E
options.text: Recurrent kidney stones and overactive bladder syndrome
options.misconception: Assumes any lower urinary tract complaint responds to finasteride.
options.explanation: Kidney stones are managed with fluids and, for distal ureteral stones, alpha blockers; overactive bladder with antimuscarinics. Finasteride shrinks the prostate and treats neither.

context: Learning objective: Finasteride is used to treat benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and male pattern hair loss.
